newsitem.title: FRANCE: French January current account surplus jumps.
newsitem.headline: French January current account surplus jumps.

text.p: France racked up a seasonally adjusted current account surplus in January of 21 billion francs, a big rise from the 10.13 billion surplus it posted in December, official figures released on Wednesday showed.
The December current account total in the balance of payments figures was revised upward sharply from the 2.43 billion francs given previously, the finance ministry said.
The revised total for the year was a record 105.21 billion francs, up from 100.68 billion announced earlier, and was the fifth annual surplus since 1992.
The unadjusted surplus for January hit a record 33.7 billion francs, up from 14.07 billion the previous month. The December unadjusted surplus had been revised upward from 13.57 billion francs.
Earlier this month, it reported a January seasonally adjusted trade surplus of 11.72 billion francs. The government has said its strong trade performance is proof of France's export competitiveness.
The ministry said it had revised the methodology used for calculating the balance of payment figures to include trade with its overseas territories of New Caledonia and French Polynesia.
Without the changes, it said the January unadjusted current account surplus of 33.7 billion francs would have been slightly higher at between 34.5 billion and 35.0 billion.
The ministry said the revisions were to conform with a European Union directive and make its figures fall in line with changes already made by the Customs Office in calculating trade data.
The ministry said it had also revised the methodology to make the balance of payments data conform to international norms and this had affected treatment of investment revenues.
Profits reinvested by overseas subsidiaries of French companies and by French subsidiaries of overseas companies were now included in investment revenues.
The financial accounts side of the balance of payments ledger showed that non-resident investors were net buyers of French government bonds in January.

The figures showed that non-residents bought a net 7.35 billion francs of government bonds in January after being net sellers the previous month. In December, they sold a net 6.08 billion francs worth of government bonds.
